properties.name: Habitat (landing site)
properties.why: Start and finish of every walk: the Octavia E. Butler landing site, where Perseverance touched down on the floor of Jezero. Routes here must return to this point, and the 1 m terrain behind them comes from MRO's HiRISE camera.

properties.name: Artuby Ridge (Rochette)
properties.why: A 2 to 3 m cliff of Máaz formation rock on the crater floor, less than 1 km from the habitat. These igneous rocks were likely lava flows, and Perseverance cored two samples here, Montdenier and Montagnac.

properties.name: Séítah olivine cumulate (Brac)
properties.why: Séítah, possibly the oldest rock on the crater floor: coarse, layered, olivine-rich rock that likely cooled from a thick lava flow, laccolith or lava lake. MRO's CRISM had mapped olivine in this region from orbit; here Perseverance sampled it up close (Salette and Coulettes).

properties.name: Delta front (Skinner Ridge)
properties.why: Where an ancient river met a lake. Jezero held a delta-lake system with high potential to preserve signs of past life, and here the rover cored layered sedimentary rock at Skinner Ridge and Wildcat Ridge (Swift Run, Skyland, Hazeltop and Bearwallow).

properties.name: Upper delta fan (Berea)
properties.why: The top of the delta holds the last chapter of water in Jezero and some of the coarsest sediments seen so far. Reaching it means climbing about 120 m above the habitat. At Berea the rover cored Melyn, from alternating layers of sandstone and coarser rock.

properties.name: Margin unit carbonates (Comet Geyser)
properties.why: The margin unit, beside the western crater rim, is where orbital spectrometers saw the strongest carbonate signal in Jezero, and it has been proposed as an ancient lake shoreline. Here the rover cored Comet Geyser, a silica-cemented carbonate.
